name: Ilhan Kyuchyuk - Projet de décision du Conseil
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the European Union, of the Council of Europe Convention on the Protection of the Environment through Criminal Law
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees that the European Union should sign up to a Council of Europe convention on fighting environmental crime through criminal law. The convention sets common international rules on what counts as a serious environmental offence, such as polluting or harming nature, and requires punishments that are effective and discourage reoffending. It also covers prevention, cross-border investigations, sharing information and collecting statistics. The Parliament's consent is the step needed for the EU to conclude the agreement.

- The EU joins a Council of Europe treaty setting shared criminal-law standards against serious environmental harm.
- It affects EU governments, courts and investigators, plus neighbouring countries that ratify it.
- After Parliament's consent, the EU can formally conclude the agreement; it enters into force after ten ratifications, at least eight from Council of Europe member states.
